ask: Amend output-never-hand-off-doable-step (do a step yourself before handing it to me) in output-styles/shiv-stylisms.md, in place, no new rule: (1) every command left to you comes as its own fenced block, ready to run as is: it starts with the cd it needs, has no placeholders for you to fill (ask first if a value is unknown), and needs no admin; (2) the shell follows where you will run it: a block for the app's Run button can be bash; a block you paste into a terminal on Windows is PowerShell (5.1-safe), since that is the terminal you open; a block that needs Git Bash says 'open Git Bash' on its first line; a Mac block is bash or zsh; never mix shells in one block, and a Mac-only or Windows-only step says which; (3) the block sits outside the report blockquote, because report-to-user-blockquote forbids code fences inside it, and the report names the block in one line. Mechanize cheaply (c26, watching costs less than what it watches): reply_judge.py, the Stop reply check that already runs, flags a reply that hands you a step with no code block. Test: a sample reply that hands off a step with no block is flagged; one with a block passes; red on main.
note: Done: landed in #560, merged Oct 22. Checked at 73ed71a: the rule already exists in shiv-stylisms.md (lines 38 to 43) and asks for a runnable bash block outside the report, but it is prose only, says nothing about PowerShell or Mac versus Windows, and sessions still skip it. So this amends that rule and adds a check, rather than adding a second rule. Gripe, Oct 21: the advisor handed you a Git Bash block, and you ran it in PowerShell, where every line failed (no grep, no bash syntax); hence the shell-follows-the-terminal clause. Can ride with the guard-rule batch (c10, c23) or the premises batch (c7, c24, c25), which edits reply hooks.
title: A step left to you comes as a command you can run with one click
why: Your ask, Oct 21: when a session won't run a command but you can, it should hand you the exact command, preferably bash, so you just press the Run button.
